A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Prior2Former and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Retained, relocated, and newly added material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original Prior2Former segmentation experiments, benchmark submissions, component ablations, and qualitative analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds a PANIC benchmark evaluation, uncertainty ablations, and mask visualizations.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the Beta-prior head, evidential sampling, symmetric Dice loss, combined uncertainty score, and thresholding followed by DBSCAN clustering. Added explanations and experimental uncertainty variants do not replace or extend the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix B.5 adds PANIC test-set evaluation on urban images from German cities at different resolutions for open-set panoptic segmentation. This extends coverage within the existing driving domain; the earlier datasets and tasks remain.

E2.justification: v2 adds Con2Mav as the PANIC comparator and additional uncertainty variants in Tables 14–15. Appendix A.1 also revises the stated RbA score from sigmoid to tanh and describes M2A global attention as complementing, rather than replacing, local attention. These are reported baseline revisions; rerunning the comparisons is not established.

E3.justification: Appendix A.4 changes the reported COCO uncertainty threshold from -0.6 to -0.55 and its DBSCAN epsilon from 0.02 to 0.1. v2 also introduces PANIC test-set evaluation and component-isolation experiments. The PDFs do not establish whether the revised COCO settings reflect reruns.

E4.justification: The uncertainty analysis expands substantially beyond v1's component ablations and predictive-versus-P2F comparison. New Tables 14–15 test alternative uncertainty constructions and isolate mask and classification contributions across anomaly and panoptic segmentation. Figure 10 and Appendix C.4 additionally examine positive and negative evidence masks.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run variability, seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added uncertainty ablations concern model predictions, not statistical uncertainty in experimental results.

E6.justification: v2 adds PANIC results, including PQ 52.9 for P2F versus 21.6 for Con2Mav, and substantial new uncertainty-ablation results in Tables 14–15. Table 2 changes EOPSN unseen-class PQ/RQ from 7.43/9.97 to 0.01/0.01, retaining SQ 74.55. Most existing P2F scores remain unchanged; the additions do not demonstrate a same-setting improvement over v1.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 changes the mathematical definition of RbA uncertainty from a negative sum of sigmoid-transformed logits in v1 Equation 19 to tanh-transformed logits in v2 Equation 16. The proposed method's prior definitions and loss equations otherwise remain mathematically equivalent, with no new proofs or theoretical results.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the same central contributions: an evidential mask transformer requiring no OOD knowledge, its loss and sampling strategy, and strong performance across the same segmentation task families. The abstract and conclusion are rephrased, but the contribution statements retain their substantive scope.

C2.justification: v1's limitations mainly emphasize the scarcity of assumption-free competitors. v2 instead explicitly acknowledges the large gap to OOD-assisted methods and difficulty calibrating uncertainty and thresholds using known classes alone. It also adds substantive interpretations of the uncertainty-component tradeoffs and the alpha/beta mask behavior.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page link and revises documented baseline implementations and COCO clustering parameters. It removes v1's explicit statement that unseen-COCO training uses 1024-by-1024 crops, reducing specificity without establishing an actual crop-size change. Most training and preprocessing details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Sodano et al.'s Open-World Panoptic Segmentation and positions the work relative to PANIC and Con2Mav. It retains the OOD-supervision rationale for excluding ContMAV but removes the earlier implementation-instability criticism. Other reference changes largely concern bibliographic metadata and formatting.

P1.justification: v2 edits prose throughout, clarifies open-set task terminology and experimental explanations, and divides Appendix C into dataset-specific subsections plus mask visualization. The main section sequence, narrative, and much of the technical text remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 12, 14, and 15 and Figure 10 while retaining the established visual structure. The old Table 12 moves to Table 13 with its TPR95 headers corrected to FPR95. Figure 5's labels and several table annotations and captions are clarified; most existing displays are preserved.

improvement.justification: The added uncertainty controls and PANIC comparison strengthen empirical support, while the rewritten limitations provide a more balanced account of performance and calibration difficulties. These benefits yield a limited overall improvement with the core method and most results retained. Unexplained COCO setting revisions, removal of the explicit unseen-training crop detail, and inconsistent sigmoid prose beside the revised tanh formula temper the reproducibility gains.
